answer.rationale: The 18% cost mandate and incumbent's refusal to renegotiate make renewal unviable. memory_c2 demonstrates that switching to a low-cost vendor achieved sharp unit cost reduction with quick onboarding and reliable invoicing—directly addressing the margin requirement. memory_c4 shows renegotiation works, but only when the incumbent is willing to move; the refusal here eliminates that path. memory_c6 proves multi-year commitments with incumbents unlock pricing, but this option is foreclosed by their stance. The assembly line's 94% utilization creates real risk: we cannot absorb supply disruption. Switching carries onboarding and integration risk, but staying incumbent without cost relief violates the mandate and leaves us exposed to margin miss. A second source (memory_c3) would hedge but not solve the cost gap in 14 days. The 14-day hard deadline forces the decision now—defer_decision defers the problem but not the cut. Verification of c2 (success case) and c4 (negotiation failure points) will confirm whether the cost vendor path is repeatable and whether negotiation is truly closed.
